Q: How do I add a variable to a dialog box (Changed add variable behaviour) A:

You're probably adding the generic "Add Member Variable" wizard instead of the control specific one. id suggest to right click the control itself in the dialog editor, and use the "Add Variable" command from the menu, that should get you the correct wizard with the correct types like CString. first It didn't work, I just cleared the IntelliSense cache and then try again.

Q: How to count number of screens via powershell or cmd A:

Count active monitors which works on Windows 11 without wmic.

@echo off
for /f %%i in ('
  powershell -noprofile -command ^
    "Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms; [System.Windows.Forms.Screen]::AllScreens.Count"
') do set n=%%i

echo %n%

Q: How can I install Eclipse and Java SDK on Ubuntu? A:

Execute this in your terminal:

sudo apt-get install eclipse
sudo apt-get install openjdk-6-jdk openjdk-6-source openjdk-6-demo openjdk-6-doc openjdk-6-jre-headless openjdk-6-jre-lib

The first one installs Eclipse (you will be asked to enter your password), and the second one installs all the Java stuff you may need!

Q: Java Decompiler with line number realignment feature for debugger compatibility A:

As Emmanuel Dupuy (@emmanue1 on GitHub) stated in his comment, the feature realigning line numbers was already in the pipe of JD projets in 2011 and it has been present in JD-Core internally for a certain number of years. Even today as of 2026, JD-Core is the only decompiler to possess this realignment feature internally.

Procyon has some experimental feature named --stretch-lines but it just moves the lines and ignores the extra work of sorting members, reversing if/else when needed, splitting static blocks to multiple locations, etc…

Fernflower didn’t have that feature because Jetbrains chose another approach with IntelliJ to make the debugger aware of the decompiler’s line number mapping in order to point it to the right location. Original developer « Stiver helped provide a transparent mapping between them so you can seamlessly debug decompiled code ». Read here.

For CFR, there’s a discussion about realigning line numbers but the author explains why he’s reluctant here.

In Eclipse Enhanced Decompiler (ECD), the realigner is a modified version of JD-Realign, and they both do some unreliable post-process, resulting sometimes in some pieces of code being cut in the process, and sometimes dozens of lines stacked into a single line (explore the issues of ECD for more details).

However, I released new plugin ECD++ on Eclipse Marketplace which uses a JAVACC parser to realign code from line numbers comments, so that it works for all decompilers, but that’s also a post-process.

Q: javax.swing does not exist A:

Read the fine manual.

  1. Specifically, read the Javadoc for the class JOptionPane.
  2. Copy-paste the fully-qualified name for that class.
  3. Paste name into your import statement.
  4. Re-compile.
import javax.swing.JOptionPane;

Read Java Tutorials by Oracle, free of charge. See simple example Swing app with an import line.

Your IDE should be helping you with this, automatically generating the import statements.

Swing has been built into every version of Java since December 8, 1998. So there is no way that JOptionPane is actually missing.

Q: Is it possible to decompile and debug Java application? A:

If the application was compiled with line number information, it's possible.

However, if all decompilers have line number mappings and the ability to write line numbers as comments, most decompilers do not handle line number realignment natively, except https://github.com/java-decompiler/jd-gui. In Preferences menu, tick checkbox Realign Line Numbers. See also my fork, line number realignment can't be perfect, and misaligned line numbers appear in red: https://github.com/nbauma109/jd-gui-duo?tab=readme-ov-file#realign-line-numbers

An Eclipse plugin introduced line number realignment as a post-decompilation process from the decompiled code: https://github.com/ecd-plugin/ecd. In Window -> Preferences menu, choose Java -> Decompiler and tick checkboxes in Debug Settings :

  • Output original line numbers as comments
  • Align code for debugging

See also my fork https://github.com/nbauma109/ecd for line number realignment with CFR decompiler and other bug fixes.

See also, this interesting thread from CFR decompiler project about a possible debug friendly output, where its author Lee Benfield explains why he's not doing the line number realignment feature : https://github.com/leibnitz27/cfr/issues/73.
